referents.why: 'Your words' (second singular genitive) inside the quotation: the psalm's addressee, God.
'You' as object of 'judged' inside the quotation: God is the one judged in the psalm.
'Never may it be' (optative): the implied subject is an impersonal 'it', the conclusion rejected in 3:3; no candidate.
'It has been written' (passive): the implied subject is the scripture, not a person; the builder's 'man' (w9) is wrong.
referents.category: impersonal passive of a quotation formula

referents.why: 'You may be justified' inside the quotation: the second person addressed in the psalm is God.
'You will prevail' inside the quotation: the addressee of the psalm, God.

links.why: The act of writing is not for the purpose; the 'so that' belongs to the quoted words. Replaced by a content link.
links.category: purpose attached to the writing formula

links.why: Same as the link to cl4: the writing formula has no purpose of its own.
links.category: purpose attached to the writing formula

links.why: The fronted-ki type is for a Hebrew ki clause; here the infinitive in en-plus-dative is a temporal adjunct ('when you are judged').
links.category: wrong link type for infinitive adjunct

links.why: The infinitive clause sits in the prepositional adjunct of cl5 as its time ('when you are judged').
'Certainly not!' is an exclamation followed by a counter-jussive; the de is not a plain 'and' that joins the two, and no link type records a rebuttal.
'Let God be true and every man [be] a liar': the two jussives are joined by de/kai.
There is no 'and' between the clause and 'just as it is written' (kathaper), which is a comparison.
'Just as it is written' declares the claim to be in accordance with the earlier written word.
'You may be justified ... and will prevail': kai joins the two in the quotation.
'It has been written' is a saying clause; the quoted words cl4 are what is said (R1).

groups.why: 'Let God be true, and every man [be] a liar' is one jussive collection with the verb elided in the second member. The builder's command=cl0 is an exclamation of denial, and 'part' is not a role of an imperative group.
A quotation of scripture introduced by 'as it is written': the formula is the frame, the quoted words are the parts. The writer is not named, so no sender.
groups.category: quotation of scripture as a writing

none_fit.where: 3:4 cl0 and cl1 ('Certainly not!' then 'let God be true')
none_fit.what: A denial followed by a counter-jussive, joined by de; no link type records a rebuttal.

cant_tell.what: 'So that you may be justified' (hopos, cl4) inside the quotation
cant_tell.why: Its purpose is an act (the man's lie) in this verse, but the form does not say which act it is for; no purpose link added.
